# A signed continuation witness for physical control

29 October 2026. Astra P1, same continuing research role.

## 1. Question and result

Can measurement, feedback, calibration, postselection, or faster switching
replace the opposing hidden responses used by the acquired cancellation
construction? A useful comparison must allow all of those ordinary routes,
not only open-loop words.

The main result here is a sufficient obstruction to exact physical control.
An analytic family of stochastic dynamics can have a nonphysical parameter
value at which all jump rates reverse sign. At that value every trajectory
ending in the opposite part of a bipartite state graph has negative weight;
every trajectory ending in the original part has positive weight. A controller
using physical trajectories and independent randomness combines these weights
positively. Analytic continuation therefore forbids a nontrivial, parameter-
independent terminal transition within a deterministic physical deadline.
It also forbids a nondegenerate exact target conditional on heralded completion
by that deadline. The negative rates are a mathematical witness, never an
available physical intervention.

For the preserved source B this applies to arbitrary continuous observation,
nonanticipating switching among all four generators, and stopping before any
fixed physical deadline. It is stronger than the earlier finite-word
exclusion. It does not exclude approximate control, a parameter actually
known to the controller, or exact endpoint control with an unbounded random
completion time. Those alternatives are constructed below and in the
complementary notes.

Combining this obstruction with the preserved source A gives an operational
separation: sources with identical complete isolated-operation baseline path
laws differ in whether useful stochastic gates can be physically completed
exactly at a fixed time, even after the excluded source is granted feedback
and switching. Actual cross-operation acquisition distinguishes their relative
responses. This is a scoped mathematical capability separation, not an
apparatus demonstration or a claim of historical priority.

# Preserved baseline preparation and the restricted native-control no-go

29 October 2026. Scope addendum to the signed-control receiving review.

The inherited warranted baseline calibration preparation remains an available
resource at its own declared interface. The signed-continuation theorem does
not question that preparation, establish its impossibility, or bootstrap it
from a later reuse claim.

The theorem concerns the same current physical device and the stated
finite-rate generator menu, with the specified unknown frozen parameter and
observation/feedback resources. A separate actual baseline initializer or a
replacement sample is outside that restricted dynamical menu. If such a
resource is available and authorized for deployment, it is a legitimate
ordinary bypass and must be included in the capability/cost comparison. It is
not made unavailable merely by calling it outside the theorem.

For example, a warranted initializer that actually delivers the desired
baseline already solves that preparation task; no native-control obstruction
can be invoked against its use. Its actual initialization or replacement
time, sensing and switching requirements, effect on the current hidden
specimen, and any locality requirements must be paid. No such deployment
latency or addressed initializer is specified by the finite-rate family used
for the signed witness.

Consequently the accepted separation is between the declared native-control
menus. It is not a dominance claim against the complete inherited acquisition
interface augmented by every warranted preparation resource. The accepted
signed-theorem SHA remains

this paragraph clarifies its boundary without altering the proof.

# Ordinary adaptive control and per-device calibration of frozen disorder

29 October 2026. Complementary Astra P1 investigation. These are strong
conventional comparators for the inherited acquired mixture construction.
Nothing here claims to invent hitting-time control, system identification,
Bernoulli factories, exact sampling or relative-entropy propagation.

## 1. What the ordinary alternative actually achieves

The inherited source B has fixed hidden h in [-1,1] and binary visible Y.
Conditional on h, one raw operation j flips Y with probability

    p0(h)=1/10+h/20,
    p1(h)=3/10+3h/20,
    p2(h)=1/4+h/10,
    p3(h)=7/20+h/10.

Each call has the same physical duration t0, and its fresh flip increment is
independent of the entire previous history conditional on h. There is no
additional unmodelled returning memory. Endpoint readout is exact and
noninvasive in the theorem. Switching, readout and randomization have actual
costs. The continuum h need not be drawn from a known prior or from equilibrium.

The declared read/choose/call interface must be an actual interface. Any
unavoidable evolution during sensing, randomization or controller latency
must be included in the native kernel or prevented by an actual holding
control. A bounded controller time alone does not imply state preservation.
Independent selector draws can be prepared before the declared input epoch;
their acquisition costs remain. The continuous generator interface in
Section 6 is an additional model promise, not inferred from endpoint data.
